label: Coordinate Geometry
overview: Coordinate geometry uses the coordinate plane to describe points, lines, and distances algebraically. SAT questions test your ability to find the distance between two points, the midpoint of a segment, and the slope of a line. These three formulas connect the geometry you see visually with the algebra you can compute.

workedExamples.problem: Points A(1, 3) and B(7, 11) are on a coordinate plane. Find the distance AB and the midpoint M.

steps.title: Compute the distance
steps.content: Use the distance formula with (x₁,y₁) = (1,3) and (x₂,y₂) = (7,11).

steps.title: Find the midpoint
steps.content: Average the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates separately.

commonMistakes.mistake: Subtracting coordinates but forgetting to square them before adding
commonMistakes.fix: The formula squares each difference: (x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)². Write the squares explicitly before taking the root.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dividing only the x-coordinates (or only y) for the midpoint

quickTip: For slope, rise is the vertical change (Δy) and run is the horizontal change (Δx). A positive slope goes up-right; negative goes down-right.
